CHAPTER 1 · ABITUR · OVERVIEW

CHAPTER 1 · ABITUR · OVERVIEW · BASIC AND ADVANCED COURSE

How the Abitur is built

If you know how the exam is built, you do not give away marks. This chapter sums up what the analysis of 16 Abitur papers from four years showed: how the marks are distributed, which types of task keep coming back and in which order it pays to practise.

16 PAPERS ANALYSED2021/22 TO 2024/25

The bar at the top shows the marks (Bewertungseinheiten, BE) in the basic course 2024/25, 80 marks in total.

STRUCTUREAS IN THE LAST FEW YEARS

1Part A and part B

PART A · WITHOUT AIDS

Only a ruler and a set square are allowed. This part is collected after a fixed time; only then does the calculator come out.

  • Basic course: 85 minutes of working time and 15 minutes to read and choose, 25 marks
  • Advanced course: 95 and 15 minutes, 30 marks

On the last page you tick which optional tasks are to be marked. If you forget, you give away marks.

PART B · WITH CALCULATOR AND FORMULA BOOKLET

The aids are a dictionary, a book of tables and formulas, drawing instruments and a graphing calculator with or without CAS. The total time including part A is 255 minutes in the basic course and 300 minutes in the advanced course.

All three compulsory tasks must be done: analysis, then analytic geometry or linear algebra, then probability and statistics. You do not choose which of the two middle tasks you write. It depends on the code number assigned to your course.

In the first three years analysis counted for almost half of all marks. In 2023/24 marks were shifted towards probability and statistics, and in 2024/25 the whole paper was cut to 80 marks in the basic course and 100 marks in the advanced course. So there is more time per mark.

TYPES OF TASKWHAT KEEPS COMING BACK

3What keeps coming back

PART A
  • Five multiple-choice questions with five answers each, in all 16 papers
  • Differentiating and integrating in your head, domain, limits
  • Short tasks: checking a point, area between parabolas, pyramid, two-way table
  • Since 2024/25 also matching graphs
PART B
  • Analysis: cubic polynomial function, parallel tangents, dividing areas, joining without a kink
  • Geometry: solids in space, equation of a plane, inclination, casting shadows
  • Linear algebra: interdependence, costs and profit, Leontief in the advanced course
  • Probability and statistics: two-way table, independence, binomial distribution, hypothesis test
KEY POINT · THE OPERATORS

State, name: the result is enough, without working.

Calculate, determine, find: the working is part of it, also in the part with a calculator.

Show, prove: the result is already given; what is asked for is the complete path to it.

Justify: with a mathematical argument, not with an example.

Assess: take a position and justify your judgement.

Interpret: the number gets its meaning in context, with a unit.

HOW TO PRACTISETHE ORDER PAYS OFF

ANALYSIS FIRST

It carries the most marks. Chapters 3 to 9 lead from investigating curves to modelling.

You can skip the chapters marked Advanced course only in the basic course.

THEN PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS

It is the most predictable. Two-way table, binomial distribution and test almost always go the same way.

Chapters 14 to 16 cover everything.

THEN COMPULSORY TASK 2

Geometry in chapters 10 and 11 or linear algebra in chapters 12 and 13, depending on your code number.

Ask your teacher if you are not sure which of the two tasks awaits you.

FINALLY

Part A in chapter 2 again and again in between. The dress rehearsal in chapter 17 runs against the clock.

Work through the dress rehearsal on paper, in one go and without the solutions.
